name: 350.org
mission: 350.org is building a global grassroots climate movement that can hold our leaders accountable to the realities of science and the principles of justice. That movement is rising from the bottom up all over the world, and is uniting to create the solutions that will ensure a better future for all. Our online campaigns, grassroots organizing, and mass public actions bring together a global network active in over 188 countries
theoryOfChange: Our strategy is twofold: resisting fossil fuel projects and its enablers, and advocating for a world powered by the sun, wind and people.

strengths_deep_dive: 350.org demonstrates a high level of institutional maturity and governance. The organization is governed by a <cite id="11">12-member board of directors</cite> and has achieved a <cite id="12">perfect 100/100 score for Leadership & Adaptability</cite> from Charity Navigator. This governance structure supports a diverse range of programs, including <cite id="13">fossil fuel divestment and climate finance advocacy</cite>. Furthermore, its grantmaking activity is substantial, distributing <cite id="14">$1,860,387 in total grants</cite> to local partners, which helps decentralize its global climate movement.
rich_narrative.summary: founded in 2008, 350.org is a global environmental advocacy organization dedicated to <cite id="1">inspiring, training, and mobilizing people</cite> to challenge systems driving climate change. The organization operates with a high degree of financial transparency, earning a <cite id="2">97/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="3">$19,507,313 in total revenue</cite> to support its mission of resisting fossil fuel projects and promoting renewable energy solutions. While its mission is global, including work in <cite id="4">India, Ukraine, and the Philippines</cite>, financial data indicates a significant concentration of resources within the United States. The organization maintains a <cite id="5">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite>, reflecting its commitment to public accountability. Its operational model focuses on <cite id="6">capacity building and movement training</cite> rather than direct service delivery. This advocacy-heavy approach is supported by a <cite id="7">program expense ratio of 81.5%</cite>, which exceeds the 75% industry benchmark for non-profits.
